title: Windows state files inherit the parent directory DACL
description: At 94b1dc6f864c064f69631d240b1e91c9bece2cdd the attacker starts as a second local Windows account that can open files under its own token. That account is not the creating user, is not a member of Administrators, and is not SYSTEM or an elevated token. Those two principals are comparable to root, which can already read the Unix 0600 files. The OS principal boundary is that second account's token against the creating user's state files. On Unix, tsk forces the state directory to 0700 and task files such as tsk.json to 0600 so another local user cannot read task data. On Windows, ensure_private_dir, create_private_file, open_lock_file, and tighten_file set no security descriptor and no mode: a missing state directory is created with create_dir_all, and tsk.json is opened with OpenOptions that apply mode 0600 only under cfg(unix). tighten_file is a no-op off Unix, including on later load, so this repository never narrows a Windows DACL after creation. src/fsperm.rs is unchanged since 8d714a201280318f92ed42d26d20bf233a1f5baf. src/store.rs moved: the Windows default is returned at lines 1432 and 1437, save calls ensure_private_dir at line 822 and tighten_state_files at line 824, and the temp document is created at line 855. The same missing descriptor covers a dispatch launcher. SystemDispatchHost::launcher_file places it at the state directory joined with launchers and a .ps1 name. On non-Unix, write_launcher creates that directory with create_dir_all and writes the script with std::fs::write, not create_private_file. That script base64-embeds profile env values and the task command arguments. config.toml temps use the same Unix-only mode. The header comment that no permission is claimed off Unix does not show whether the inherited parent DACL already excludes that second account. The installer creates %LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\tsk\bin and does not create or ACL the state directory. A second non-admin local account might read %LOCALAPPDATA%\tsk\tsk.json, or a launcher script already stored beside it, if that inherited DACL allows it. Plaintext readable only by the creating account would not cross this boundary. Source cannot show the inherited DACL.
claimed_root_cause: ensure_private_dir, create_private_file, open_lock_file, and tighten_file apply owner-only mode bits only on Unix. On Windows they create the state directory and task files through std::fs with no security descriptor and never call a DACL API, so the directory and tsk.json keep the parent directory's inherited DACL and are not tightened later. SystemDispatchHost::write_launcher on non-Unix is the same gap: it creates the launchers directory with create_dir_all and writes the PowerShell launcher with std::fs::write, not create_private_file, so that file also receives no security descriptor. create_private_temp does the same for config.toml.

trace.description: When TSK_STATE_DIR is unset and LOCALAPPDATA is non-empty, the Windows default is that directory joined with tsk. Line 1432 returns PathBuf::from(local).join("tsk"). Lines 1435-1437 fall back to USERPROFILE joined with .tsk when LOCALAPPDATA is empty.
Each supported save calls ensure_private_dir on the state directory at line 822, then tighten_state_files at line 824, before replacing tsk.json.
A missing directory is created with fs::create_dir_all. The Windows-only extra step is reject_reparse_ancestors at lines 35-36. tighten_private_dir, which applies 0700, is cfg(unix) at lines 55-56.

Each existing private state name, including tsk.json, is passed to tighten_file at line 1185. Load at line 749 and save at line 824 both call this function, so a later load is the same no-op off Unix.
The cfg(not(unix)) body at lines 300-303 discards the path. No mode bits and no security descriptor are written.

The temp document is opened with filesystem.create_file. StdFilesystem::create_file at line 319 calls create_private_file. tighten_state_files has already returned at line 824 and does not run again after this create.
OpenOptions is write, create, and truncate at line 175, then open. mode(0o600) exists only inside cfg(unix) at lines 176-179. The Windows open passes no security descriptor.
Separate from the tsk.json replace, a dispatch launcher is the state directory joined with launchers and the workspace file name. The script therefore lives under the same state directory.

The cfg(not(unix)) body creates the launchers directory with std::fs::create_dir_all and writes the script with std::fs::write. It does not call create_private_file. The Unix body at lines 1825-1831 does. The Windows write passes no security descriptor, and nothing later calls tighten_file on the .ps1.

evidence.description: The module header says Unix state directories are 0700 and files are 0600, and that no permission is claimed on other platforms, where these helpers compile down to plain create and copy.
Before create_dir_all, Windows only calls reject_reparse_ancestors. The directory create attaches no security descriptor.
The directory tighten call is gated by cfg(unix); the Windows function returns after the reparse and directory checks.
options.mode(0o600) is inside the cfg(unix) block that begins at line 176.

open_lock_file sets mode 0600 only inside the cfg(unix) block at lines 244-248. The Windows open passes no security descriptor. Callers at store.rs lines 885 and 1118 then call tighten_file, which does not change a Windows DACL.
Under cfg(not(unix)), tighten_file ignores its path. An existing Windows state file is not given an owner-only DACL.
The production AtomicFilesystem create_file implementation is create_private_file, with no Windows security-attribute argument.
Load calls tighten_state_files, which is a no-op off Unix.
The non-empty LOCALAPPDATA branch returns PathBuf::from(local).join("tsk").
When LOCALAPPDATA is unavailable, the Windows fallback returns PathBuf::from(userprofile).join(".tsk").
launcher_file joins the host state directory with launchers. The production write at line 1821 uses that path.
On non-Unix, write_launcher uses std::fs::create_dir_all and std::fs::write. The Unix branch above it uses ensure_private_dir and create_private_file because the launcher carries profile env values.
powershell_script base64-embeds each profile env value, then the command arguments, into the script write_launcher stores.
create_private_temp, used for config.toml, opens with create_new and applies mode 0600 only inside cfg(unix) at this line, then opens with no security descriptor on Windows.
The storage guide documents the Windows default as LOCALAPPDATA\tsk, or USERPROFILE\.tsk when LOCALAPPDATA is unavailable, and does not document a Windows ACL.
The Windows installer default directory is LOCALAPPDATA joined with Programs\tsk\bin. That is the program directory, not the state directory.
The installer creates that program directory with New-Item. The repository contains no DACL, icacls, or Set-Acl call, so the installer does not ACL the state directory.

blockers: The inherited DACL is an operating-system fact. This repository never sets or records a Windows security descriptor. ensure_private_dir, create_private_file, open_lock_file, tighten_file, create_private_temp, and the non-Unix write_launcher path all leave it unset, so source cannot show whether a second non-admin account, which is not the owner and not Administrators or SYSTEM, has an allow ACE on the state directory, tsk.json, or a launcher script.
A Windows DACL observation is required and was not performed. This host is Linux, so it cannot create a Windows profile or query a DACL, and target code was not executed.

validation_plan.local: On a fresh Windows 10 or 11 profile that is not a member of Administrators and is not elevated, leave TSK_STATE_DIR unset and do not pass --state-dir. Run tsk add with a dummy title so the default state directory and tsk.json are created. Do not dispatch and do not create a worktree. As that same user, run icacls with only the path, and no /grant, /deny, /remove, /reset, /setowner, /inheritance, /restore, or /replace, on %LOCALAPPDATA%\tsk and on %LOCALAPPDATA%\tsk\tsk.json and record every ACE and inheritance flag. If LOCALAPPDATA was unset, use %USERPROFILE%\.tsk instead. If a .ps1 is already present under that directory's launchers folder, run the same path-only icacls on that one file and on its launchers directory, and do not delete or edit it. From a second local account that is also not a member of Administrators, not SYSTEM, and not elevated, attempt only to read the state directory and tsk.json, and the existing launcher file when one was recorded, and stop at access denied or at seeing the dummy text. Do not take ownership, change the ACL, or use an elevated token. If that second account can read the dummy text, the boundary the Unix build enforces with 0700 and 0600 is crossed for the state file, and a launcher written later with no security descriptor inherits that same parent DACL. If access is denied and the DACL allows only the creating user, SYSTEM, and Administrators, the inherited DACL already matches that account boundary.
validation_plan.deployment: On an existing Windows store, run icacls with only the path on the state directory, on tsk.json, and, when present, on the launchers directory and one existing .ps1 under it. Do not change the ACL, do not take ownership, do not dispatch, and do not open the task file or the launcher. Record whether any allow ACE, including an inherited ACE, grants read to a principal other than the owner, SYSTEM, and Administrators. Stop after recording the DACL.
